clue.text: Rower uses river to enter city that lies on one

indicators.note: the river's abbreviation goes into the middle of the city's name, so entering means placing inside

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent is named for lying on a river, the Trent

explanation.surface: An oarsman takes the river into a city built on its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: STOKE-on-Trent is an English city on the River Trent. In a rowing eight the stroke is the rower who sets the pace.
explanation.definitionFit: In a racing boat the stroke is the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the rhythm for the crew.

clue.text: go to American university

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'go to American university (6)', cut short in OCR; the blog prints 'Put in vehicle that's turned up to go to American University' (BUS reversed + MIT), but no scan is available to confirm the repair.

clue.text: Supporter in Romania meeting broadcaster Kate

parts.note: RO is the international vehicle code for Romania
Kate Adie is a well-known BBC news correspondent

explanation.surface: A fan in Bucharest bumps into a famous television reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate ADIE was the BBC's chief news correspondent for many years, a household name in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie supports a touring band, carrying and setting up its equipment.

clue.text: Soldier in uniform joining any number in shout of acclamation

parts.note: kit is a set of clothing, as in a sports or army uniform

indicators.note: the letter for a number sits inside the word for a shout, so in means placed within

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of approval
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A soldier in uniform joins a crowd cheering him on.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was the British field marshal of the First World War recruiting posters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchener was a famous British field marshal and war secretary, a military man.

clue.text: Put off region, not one for adult to dwell in

indicators.note: the letter for an adult goes to live inside the shortened word, so dwelling in means placing within
not tells us to take the letter for one away from the region word

parts.note: a district is an area or region
I is the Roman numeral for one
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Someone postpones a visit to a region unsuitable for grown-ups to live in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the I from DISTRICT, leaving DISTRCT; 'to dwell in' puts A into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To distract someone is to divert or put them off what they are doing.

clue.text: Doctor to patronise offensively

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with or alter it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a physician not to talk down to patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the anagram signal for TO PATRONISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in poor taste means behaving in a vulgar or offensive manner.

clue.text: The service he's walked out of — it's banal

indicators.note: the letters of he leave the phrase, as someone walking out of a room leaves it

parts.note: a rite is a religious ceremony or service

explanation.surface: A man storms out of a church service, finding it dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a worshipper storming out; in fact 'walked out of' just strips HE from 'The'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite and banal both describe remarks that are stale and unoriginal.

clue.text: Creative type who brings things alive

definitions.text: Creative type who brings things alive

parts.words: Creative type who brings things alive
parts.note: an artist whose drawings or models are made to move on screen, given an illusion of life

explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon artist makes still drawings appear to move, giving them life on screen.

clue.text: Like some decorations put on sale with small edging round

indicators.note: the word for small goes around the outside of the selling word, framing it like an edge

parts.note: tiny means very small
to sell is to offer goods for sale

explanation.surface: Christmas ornaments are marked for sale with a little trim around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with small edging round' reads as a decoration trimmed at the edges, but 'edging round' means the word for small encloses the sale word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinselly describes the glittery strands used for Christmas decorating.

clue.text: Be sitting beside nameless relation, very attractive lady

indicators.note: without a name means the letter N, abbreviation for name, is dropped

parts.note: an aunty is a relative

explanation.surface: A girl sits next to her aunt, who is stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops N, the usual abbreviation for name; 'very' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty is a woman of striking good looks.

clue.text: Reptile concealed behind river retreating when spotted by Scot

indicators.note: behind places the concealed word after the turned river rather than before it
retreating means going backwards, so the river's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
hid means concealed
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A snake hides behind a river until a Scotsman notices it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the Italian river backwards. Ophidian, usually an adjective, serves here as a noun meaning a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophidian means belonging to the snake family, so a snake, which is a reptile.

clue.text: Flower girl pursued by Henry in Cork?

parts.note: Iris is both a flower and a girl's name
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A florist's assistant is chased by a man named Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork is a city in Ireland, so anything in Cork is Irish; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cork is a city in the Republic of Ireland, so its things are Irish.

clue.text: One managing to eat egg had meal to fit in with others

indicators.note: the word for one who copes swallows the egg letter, so eating means containing

parts.note: a coper is someone who copes or manages
O looks like an egg
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: Someone eats an egg and has a meal so as to fit in with the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One managing' looks like a business manager, but here it is someone who copes; 'to eat' signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to work together harmoniously with others.

clue.text: Racehorse -it could have been trained for them?

definitions.text: Racehorse -it could have been trained for them?

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are reworked into a new shape, so this signals an anagram

explanation.surface: A racehorse might have been trained for people who drive chariots.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RACEHORSE IT rearrange to the answer, and the whole clue describes those who would train horses for racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Charioteers drove horse-drawn chariots in races, so a trained racehorse would suit them.

clue.text: Place where youngsters learn something — cannot, if hols have been arranged

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Children can't learn anything if the holidays are fixed for term time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hols' is British slang for holidays. An infant school in Britain takes pupils aged about four to seven.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant school is a British primary school for the youngest children.

clue.text: Sort of design used in fancy linos once

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, suggesting the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A decorative pattern was once used on elaborate linoleum flooring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' is the anagram signal for LINOS ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloisonne is an enamelling technique creating patterns in wire-bounded cells.

clue.text: Young female writer wants the minimum of time to be wasted

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: the smallest possible portion of time is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl writing feels that even a moment of her time is wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the minimum of' takes just the first letter of 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspent means squandered, as of a misspent youth.

clue.text: Normally reliable type has broken law in sudden movement

indicators.note: the scrambled law goes inside the jolt word, so in means placed within

parts.note: a start is a sudden jerk of surprise

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters of law are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dependable person breaks the law in a sudden moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a criminal; 'broken' is the anagram signal for law, and 'in' places the result inside the startled jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a loyal, dependable supporter.

clue.text: Break during academic period — is boy one to be kept in?

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a term is a division of the school year

indicators.note: the letter for one is held inside the boy word, so kept in means contained

parts.note: a son is a boy child
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: During term a pupil asks whether a boy is to be kept in at break.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a teacher deciding on detention at playtime; 'to be kept in' signals the Roman one going inside the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermission is an interval or pause, as in a play.

clue.text: Fellow with nothing goes across Spain — it's certainly not expensive

indicators.note: the fellow and the zero span the country letter, sitting on either side of it

parts.note: a chap is a man or fellow
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A penniless man travels across Spain on a budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes across' puts CHAP+O around E: CH-E-AP-O.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapo is informal for something low-cost and inferior.

clue.text: Sailor off with the fairies and not on his ship?

parts.note: AB is able-bodied seaman
sent is slang for blissfully transported, carried away in a dream

explanation.surface: A daydreaming sailor is missing from his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off with the fairies' is a British idiom for being in a dream world; the question mark flags a definition fitted to the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor missing from his vessel is away, not present aboard.

clue.text: Chemical splattered around-absorbed finally for removal

indicators.note: around suggests letters moved about, so the fodder is rearranged
finally picks the closing letter of the word absorbed

explanation.surface: A chemical splashed about is soaked up before being cleared away.
explanation.walkthrough: SPLATTERED rearranged, with D (the last letter of 'absorbed') taken out for removal, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, a compound used in gunpowder.

clue.text: Dwarf planet that is submerged under water

definitions.meaning: the former ninth planet, reclassified in 2006
the Second World War fuel pipeline laid beneath the English Channel

explanation.definitionFit: Both the demoted dwarf world and the wartime Channel fuel line, Pipe-Line Under The Ocean, share this name.

clue.text: Term of respect in a greeting received by British Society looking back

indicators.note: the outer pair take the inner letters in, as a host receives guests
looking back means read backwards, so the two abbreviations reverse

parts.note: hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A respectful greeting is given to a society looking back on Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: B+S reversed ('looking back') gives SB, which holds A+HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was a respectful form of address used in colonial India.

clue.text: Acts of destruction certain to occur in particular times

indicators.note: the certain word happens inside the periods word, so it is placed within

parts.note: eras are distinctive periods of history
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Destruction is sure to happen at certain moments in history.
explanation.walkthrough: ERAS holds SURE: ERA-SURE-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasures are deletions, the wiping out of written marks.

clue.text: Tie man in knots — you want him to escape

indicators.note: tied in knots means twisted up, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner is tied up, though you'd hope he gets free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in knots' scrambles TIE MAN. The definition is cryptic: a prisoner you sympathise with.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a prisoner, someone who would wish to break out of jail.

clue.text: Small bird caught finally with rodent eating it

indicators.note: the letter and rodent take in the little word, so eating means containing
finally picks the last letter of the word caught

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: A small bird is caught at last by a mouse that eats it.
explanation.walkthrough: T (last of 'caught') and MOUSE surround IT ('eating').
explanation.definitionFit: A titmouse is a tit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Holiday location put in order again?

definitions.meaning: a seaside or ski destination for vacations

explanation.definitionFit: A holiday destination is a resort, and to arrange anew is to re-sort, a pun on the hyphenated form.
